title: Play two keys an octave apart as one chord: press both at the same moment, one hand on each, and hold them
instruction: Press the two keys marked with red dots at the same moment, one hand on each, hold them down together for a second, and press no other key.
context: Pianists often play the same note in two octaves, one hand on each, to make it sound full: the two keys must go down together, or they sound as two notes. Two keys 21 cm apart, far wider than one hand spans, test the timing of two hands working together.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. A fixed toy keyboard (a dark case with a raised back and two knobs), its keys running away from the arms: fifteen white keys from G to G, each 2.9 cm wide (3 cm apart) and 15 cm long, their front edges 23.5 cm forward and their tops 4.5 cm above the table, spanning from 21 cm left to 24 cm right of the centre line; the black keys stand between them over the back 55% of the white keys, 1 cm higher. Each white key is hinged at its back end on a spring: its front goes down at most 8 mm (pressed on its dot, about 0.8 N to start and 1.2 N fully down). The two C keys, 10.5 cm left and 10.5 cm right of the centre line, carry red dots 2 cm from their front edge. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: A key is down with its front pressed at least 5 mm. Played: both marked keys go down within 0.1 s of each other and stay down together for 1 s. 1.0: played; 0.5: both held down together for 1 s, but they went down more than 0.1 s apart; 0.25: one of them held down for 1 s; any other white key pressed down at any time caps the score at 0.25; else 0.0. The best moment of the trial counts. The trial ends at the run limit, or 1 s after the chord is played.
reset_notes: Nothing to put back: let go of the keys and they spring back up.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: each white key is a rigid bar on a sprung hinge at its back end, stopped 8 mm down at its front; no sound, no hammers or key action. The black keys are fixed (not playable) and the keyboard is fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
